pdfReferences.section: Introduction to DBMS & SQL Server
Introduction to DBMS & SQL Server

prerequisites: Basic computer literacy and understanding of files
learningObjectives: Explain file management system drawbacks and the necessity of modern DBMS
Differentiate Network, Hierarchical, and Relational (RDBMS) systems
Configure SQL Server Management Studio (SSMS) and understand Windows vs. SQL Authentication
Describe SQL Server storage internals: data files (.mdf/.ndf), log files (.ldf), pages, and extents
days.the8020Knowledge: Databases organize data into 8KB physical storage pages grouped into 64KB extents. Write operations hit the transaction log (.ldf) first before committing to data files (.mdf), guaranteeing ACID reliability.
days.whatExpertsUnderstand: Understanding page allocation and log file write-ahead logging (WAL) separates database developers from casual query writers. It explains checkpoint overhead, transaction log growth, and query I/O cost.

topicExplanation.whatIsIt: A Relational Database Management System (RDBMS) is structured software that stores, retrieves, and enforces integrity on business data using relational tables with rows and columns.
topicExplanation.whyLearnIt: Every enterprise data platform, data pipeline in Azure, and Power BI report ultimately ingests data originating from relational databases.
coreConcepts: Drawbacks of File Management Systems (data redundancy, lack of concurrency, zero integrity enforcement)
DBMS Evolution: Hierarchical (tree-based) vs Network (graph-based) vs Relational (tuple-relation based)
SQL Server Architecture: Protocol Layer, Relational Engine (Query Parser, Optimizer), Storage Engine (Buffer Pool, Access Methods)
Connecting to Server & Authentication Modes: Windows Integrated Authentication (Kerberos/NTLM) vs Mixed Mode SQL Authentication
topicExplanation.importantTechnicalDetails: Storage allocation: 1 Page = 8 KB (8192 bytes); 1 Extent = 8 contiguous pages (64 KB). Mixed extents hold multiple objects; Uniform extents belong to a single object.
topicExplanation.realWorldApplication: Configuring a production database storage layout on separate NVMe disk volumes for .mdf (data) and .ldf (transaction logs) to avoid disk I/O bottlenecks.
topicExplanation.commonMistakes: Putting both data and log files on the same disk drive, or setting transaction log autogrowth to tiny 1MB increments which causes severe virtual log file (VLF) fragmentation.
topicExplanation.quickRevision: RDBMS solves file system limitations with ACID compliance. SQL Server stores data in 8KB pages. SSMS is the management interface.
topicExplanation.whatYouShouldBeAbleToDo: Install SSMS, connect to a local or remote SQL Server instance, and explain the physical filegroup structure of a database.

codeExample.title: Creating Database with Custom File Architecture
codeExample.code:
CREATE DATABASE CorporateDW
ON PRIMARY (
    NAME = CorporateDW_Data,
    FILENAME = 'C:\SQLData\CorporateDW.mdf',
    SIZE = 50MB,
    MAXSIZE = 5GB,
    FILEGROWTH = 64MB
)
LOG ON (
    NAME = CorporateDW_Log,
    FILENAME = 'C:\SQLLog\CorporateDW.ldf',
    SIZE = 25MB,
    MAXSIZE = 1GB,
    FILEGROWTH = 32MB
);
codeExample.explanation: Explicitly sets initial file sizes and fixed megabyte autogrowth to prevent Virtual Log File fragmentation.

interviewQuestions.question: What is the difference between a page and an extent in SQL Server?
interviewQuestions.answer: A page is the fundamental unit of data storage in SQL Server, sized at 8 KB. An extent is a collection of eight physically contiguous pages (64 KB). SQL Server allocates storage in extents.
interviewQuestions.whyInterviewerAsks: Tests whether the candidate understands internal storage architecture rather than just surface-level SQL syntax.

interviewQuestions.question: Why should data files (.mdf) and transaction log files (.ldf) be separated physically in production?
interviewQuestions.answer: Data file operations are predominantly random I/O (reads and checkpoint writes), whereas transaction log operations are strictly sequential writes. Placing them on separate storage drives avoids I/O head contention and guarantees write-ahead logging performance.
interviewQuestions.whyInterviewerAsks: Evaluates production database administration awareness.

quiz.question: What is the physical size of a single data page in Microsoft SQL Server?
quiz.explanation: SQL Server data pages are fixed at 8 KB (8192 bytes). Eight contiguous pages form a 64 KB extent.

quiz.question: Which file extension is traditionally used for SQL Server secondary data files?
quiz.explanation: .mdf is the primary data file, .ldf is the transaction log file, and .ndf is for secondary data files.

quiz.question: What is the main purpose of the transaction log (.ldf)?
options: Records all database modifications before they are written to data files for ACID recovery
quiz.explanation: The transaction log enables write-ahead logging (WAL), guaranteeing durability and point-in-time recovery.

pdfReferences.section: SQL Server Data Types & Business Integrity
SQL Server Data Types

learningObjectives: Differentiate Unicode (NCHAR, NVARCHAR) vs Non-Unicode (CHAR, VARCHAR) and storage impact
Select optimal data types for numerical, currency, datetime, GUID, and binary data
Implement business integrity constraints: PRIMARY KEY, FOREIGN KEY, UNIQUE, CHECK, DEFAULT, NOT NULL
Understand identity columns and surrogate key generation in relational schema design
days.the8020Knowledge: Non-Unicode (VARCHAR) uses 1 byte per character, while Unicode (NVARCHAR) uses 2 bytes per character to support international scripts. Primary Keys enforce entity integrity; Foreign Keys enforce referential integrity.
days.whatExpertsUnderstand: Choosing NVARCHAR when VARCHAR suffices doubles the memory buffer pool footprint and network serialization payload. Using INT or BIGINT identity keys instead of GUIDs for clustered keys prevents index fragmentation.

topicExplanation.whatIsIt: Data types define the storage size, format, and allowable values for column data. Business integrity constraints enforce business rules directly at the database level to prevent corrupt or orphan data.
topicExplanation.whyLearnIt: Dirty, unconstrained data in source tables causes pipeline failures in Azure Data Factory and incorrect aggregations in Power BI.
coreConcepts: Unicode (NCHAR, NVARCHAR, NVARCHAR(MAX)) vs Non-Unicode (CHAR, VARCHAR, VARCHAR(MAX))
Exact Numerics (INT, BIGINT, DECIMAL(p,s), NUMERIC) vs Approximate (FLOAT, REAL)
Temporal types: DATE, DATETIME2(p), TIME, DATETIMEOFFSET
Integrity Constraints: PRIMARY KEY, FOREIGN KEY with ON DELETE/UPDATE rules, UNIQUE, CHECK, DEFAULT
topicExplanation.importantTechnicalDetails: DECIMAL(10,2) allocates 5 bytes (10 digits total, 2 after decimal). DATETIME2(3) uses 7 bytes with 1ms precision, replacing legacy DATETIME (8 bytes with 3.33ms rounding flaw).
topicExplanation.realWorldApplication: Enforcing referential integrity between an OrderHeader and OrderDetails table so orphan line items cannot be saved without an existing order header.
topicExplanation.commonMistakes: Using FLOAT for financial balances (leading to floating-point rounding errors) instead of DECIMAL(18,2).
topicExplanation.quickRevision: VARCHAR for single-byte English text, NVARCHAR for multi-lingual text. Constraints enforce business logic natively.
topicExplanation.whatYouShouldBeAbleToDo: Design a normalized database schema with primary keys, foreign keys, check constraints, and optimal data types.

codeExample.title: Schema Definition with Business Integrity Constraints
codeExample.code:
CREATE TABLE Customers (
    CustomerID INT IDENTITY(1,1) PRIMARY KEY,
    CustomerCode VARCHAR(20) NOT NULL UNIQUE,
    FullName NVARCHAR(100) NOT NULL,
    Email VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,
    CreatedDate DATETIME2(0) DEFAULT SYSDATETIME()
);

CREATE TABLE Orders (
    OrderID BIGINT IDENTITY(1000,1) PRIMARY KEY,
    CustomerID INT NOT NULL,
    OrderDate DATETIME2(0) DEFAULT SYSDATETIME(),
    TotalAmount DECIMAL(12,2) NOT NULL CHECK (TotalAmount >= 0),
    Status VARCHAR(20) DEFAULT 'Pending' CHECK (Status IN ('Pending', 'Processing', 'Shipped', 'Delivered')),
    CONSTRAINT FK_Orders_Customers FOREIGN KEY (CustomerID) REFERENCES Customers(CustomerID)
);

interviewQuestions.question: What is the difference between VARCHAR and NVARCHAR in SQL Server?
interviewQuestions.answer: VARCHAR stores single-byte Non-Unicode characters (ASCII/code-page), using 1 byte per character. NVARCHAR stores double-byte Unicode characters (UTF-16), using 2 bytes per character. NVARCHAR supports all international scripts, but consumes double the storage.
interviewQuestions.whyInterviewerAsks: Checks storage awareness and character encoding fundamentals.

interviewQuestions.question: Can a table have multiple UNIQUE constraints and multiple PRIMARY KEYs?
interviewQuestions.answer: A table can have only ONE Primary Key, but it can have multiple UNIQUE constraints. Primary Keys cannot accept NULL values, while a UNIQUE constraint in SQL Server permits a single NULL value.
interviewQuestions.whyInterviewerAsks: Tests understanding of relational integrity rules.

quiz.question: How many bytes of storage does an INT data type consume in SQL Server?
quiz.explanation: INT is a 4-byte integer spanning from -2,147,483,648 to 2,147,483,647. BIGINT consumes 8 bytes.

quiz.question: Which constraint ensures that a column does not accept duplicate values and cannot be NULL?
quiz.explanation: A Primary Key uniquely identifies each row and strictly disallows NULL values.

quiz.question: What happens when you define a column as DECIMAL(10,2)?
options: Maximum 10 digits total, with 2 digits after the decimal point
quiz.explanation: Precision (10) is the total number of digits; Scale (2) is the number of digits to the right of the decimal point.

pdfReferences.section: Queries
Queries

learningObjectives: Master logical query processing order: FROM -> WHERE -> GROUP BY -> HAVING -> SELECT -> ORDER BY
Implement all join types: INNER, LEFT/RIGHT OUTER, FULL OUTER, CROSS JOIN, and SELF JOIN
Write multi-level aggregations using GROUP BY, HAVING, and set operators (UNION, UNION ALL, INTERSECT, EXCEPT)
Develop correlated and nested subqueries with EXISTS and NOT EXISTS predicates
days.the8020Knowledge: Understanding the true logical processing order of SQL execution prevents 90% of beginner errors (like attempting to filter column aliases in the WHERE clause). INNER JOIN returns matches; LEFT JOIN keeps all left rows.
days.whatExpertsUnderstand: EXISTS performs short-circuit evaluation stopping at the first match, making it significantly faster than IN for subquery existence checks against large datasets.

topicExplanation.whatIsIt: Data Query Language (DQL) allows retrieving, transforming, and filtering data from multiple relational tables using mathematical set operations and predicate logic.
topicExplanation.whyLearnIt: Writing performant SQL queries is the #1 mandatory skill for data engineers and BI developers. Bad queries stall pipelines and bloat cloud data warehouse bills.
coreConcepts: Logical Query Processing Order (why SELECT executes after WHERE and GROUP BY)
Relational Joins: Inner, Left/Right Outer, Full Outer, Cross Join (Cartesian Product), Self Join
Group-level Aggregations: SUM, COUNT, AVG, MIN, MAX combined with HAVING filtering
Subquery Varieties: Scalar Subqueries, Multi-row Subqueries, Correlated Subqueries, EXISTS vs IN
Set Operators: UNION (distinct) vs UNION ALL (preserves duplicates), INTERSECT, EXCEPT
topicExplanation.importantTechnicalDetails: UNION removes duplicates by sorting the combined dataset (high memory/CPU cost). UNION ALL simply concatenates result sets without sorting.
topicExplanation.realWorldApplication: Extracting customer lifetime value and latest order status by joining Customers, Orders, and Payments tables with aggregate GROUP BY logic.
topicExplanation.commonMistakes: Using HAVING instead of WHERE for row-level filters, or using IN with a subquery that might return a NULL (which causes NOT IN to return zero rows).
topicExplanation.quickRevision: Logical order: FROM -> WHERE -> GROUP BY -> HAVING -> SELECT -> ORDER BY. Use UNION ALL unless distinct deduplication is explicitly required.
topicExplanation.whatYouShouldBeAbleToDo: Write complex analytical SQL queries joining 3+ tables with filtering, aggregation, and subqueries.

codeExample.title: Analytical Multi-Table Query with Joins & Aggregations
codeExample.code:
-- High-value customers with total spend and recent activity
SELECT 
    c.CustomerID,
    c.FullName,
    COUNT(o.OrderID) AS TotalOrders,
    SUM(o.TotalAmount) AS TotalSpent,
    MAX(o.OrderDate) AS LastOrderDate
FROM Customers c
INNER JOIN Orders o ON c.CustomerID = o.CustomerID
WHERE o.OrderDate >= DATEADD(DAY, -90, SYSDATETIME())
GROUP BY c.CustomerID, c.FullName
HAVING SUM(o.TotalAmount) > 1000
ORDER BY TotalSpent DESC;

-- Inactive customers using Anti-Join pattern
SELECT c.CustomerID, c.FullName, c.Email
FROM Customers c
LEFT JOIN Orders o ON c.CustomerID = o.CustomerID
WHERE o.OrderID IS NULL;

interviewQuestions.question: What is the difference between WHERE and HAVING in SQL?
interviewQuestions.answer: WHERE filters individual rows BEFORE any grouping or aggregation takes place. HAVING filters aggregated groups AFTER the GROUP BY operation has executed.
interviewQuestions.whyInterviewerAsks: Checks if the candidate understands the logical execution flow of SQL.

interviewQuestions.question: Why is UNION ALL generally faster than UNION?
interviewQuestions.answer: UNION performs a distinct sort across the combined result set to identify and eliminate duplicate rows, which requires significant memory and tempdb spills. UNION ALL directly concatenates the result streams without sorting or deduplication.
interviewQuestions.whyInterviewerAsks: Evaluates query performance awareness.

quiz.question: Which SQL clause executes first in logical query processing?
quiz.explanation: FROM is the first logical clause evaluated, identifying and joining source tables before WHERE filters rows.

quiz.question: What is the result of a CROSS JOIN between a table with 5 rows and a table with 10 rows?
quiz.explanation: CROSS JOIN produces a Cartesian product (5 x 10 = 50 rows).

quiz.question: Why might 'NOT IN (subquery)' return 0 rows unexpectedly?
options: The subquery result contains at least one NULL value
The table lacks a primary key
The database is in read-only mode
quiz.explanation: If any value returned by the subquery is NULL, the comparison evaluated against NULL yields UNKNOWN, causing NOT IN to return zero rows.

Understand the difference between WHERE and HAVING
Use EXISTS instead of IN for correlated subqueries
